title: John Glenn
summary: This document is a comprehensive biographical article about John Glenn (1921–2016), the American Marine Corps aviator, NASA astronaut, and U.S. Senator from Ohio. The document begins with an overview of Glenn's life, highlighting his historic achievements as the third American in space and the first to orbit the Earth aboard Friendship 7 in 1962, his 24-year Senate career, and his return to space at age 77. The article then details his early life and education in Ohio, where he met his future wife Annie and developed a passion for aviation. A substantial section covers his military career, including his World War II combat service in the Pacific, his Korean War service during which he shot down three MiG-15s and flew alongside baseball star Ted Williams, and his work as a test pilot, including his record-setting 1957 supersonic transcontinental flight ("Project Bullet"). The NASA career section describes his selection as one of the original Mercury Seven astronauts, the famous Friendship 7 orbital flight with its tense heat shield scare, his emergence as a national hero, and his controversial opposition to women astronauts. The political sections chronicle his multiple Senate campaigns—including a failed 1964 bid, a 1970 primary loss, his successful 1974, 1980, 1986, and 1992 campaigns, his unsuccessful 1984 presidential run, and his 1976 vice presidential consideration—along with his Senate work on nuclear non-proliferation, government waste reduction, and the Keating Five scandal. The document also covers his 1998 return to space aboard STS-95 as a research subject for aging studies, his personal life including his 73-year marriage and religious faith, his 2016 death at age 95, and the extensive awards, honors, and namesakes (such as the Glenn Research Center and John Glenn Columbus International Airport) commemorating his legacy.
